Patroha Jewish Cemetery 1

Jewish Cemetery · Pátroha, Hungary

Not demolished. One of two Jewish cemeteries in Pátroha, appearing on an 1870 cadastral map with tombstones through 1940. Though undocumented when Jews first settled, the village had a notably significant Jewish community by the late 17th century compared to neighboring villages - 24 Jews across 4 families by 1770, initially working nobility-owned wineries before shifting mainly to trade. Under Kisvárda's rabbinate, the community reached 107 (of 3,180 residents) by 1941, the same year its youth were sent to forced labor battalions. Residents were confined to the Kisvárda Ghetto alongside neighboring towns' Jews, marked for collection at a roadside crucifix where local gendarmes robbed them en route; by month's end in May 1944, survivors were deported to Auschwitz. Only 11 Jews remained in the settlement by 1949.
